sources.name: AQA English Literature: modern texts and poetry

resources.statusNote: These are the school's choices from AQA's lists. Literature is closed book: no text is given in the exam except the extract, the named poem and the unseen poems.

blocks.title: Your set texts
rows: Paper 1, Section A: one question. Write about the printed extract, then about the whole play
Macbeth, Lady Macbeth, Banquo, Macduff, Duncan, the witches
ambition, power and kingship, guilt, the supernatural, appearance and reality
*The Strange Case of Dr Jekyll and Mr Hyde*
Paper 1, Section B: one question. Write about the printed extract, then about the whole novel
duality, secrecy, science, reputation, religion and sin
J. B. Priestley, written in 1945 and set in 1912
Paper 2, Section A: one essay from a choice of two
the Inspector, Eva Smith, the Birlings, Gerald Croft
Paper 2, Section B: compare a named poem with one other
poems you have not read before
Paper 2, Section C: two questions. One on an unseen poem, then one comparing it with a second unseen poem
blocks.note: Paper 1 is 1 hour 45 minutes, 64 marks and 40% of the GCSE. Paper 2 is 2 hours 15 minutes, 96 marks and 60%.

applications.title: Why these stories last
applications.body: Macbeth's ambition, Jekyll's double life and the older Birlings' refusal to take responsibility are still how people argue about leaders, secrets and society today.

applications.title: Plays in performance
applications.body: *An Inspector Calls* and *Macbeth* are staged somewhere most years; seeing a production, or a filmed one, shows choices a reader cannot see on the page.

resources.title: Power and Conflict poems
resources.summary: The fifteen poems of the Power and Conflict cluster with their poets, grouped the way this app teaches them, so you can see at a glance which poems pair well for a comparison.

blocks.title: Fifteen poems, four groups
rows: The Charge of the Light Brigade
blocks.note: The exam prints one named poem and asks you to compare it with **one other of your choice** from the cluster. Pairing within a group is safest; the best comparisons also cross groups.

applications.title: Poems about now
applications.body: *Remains* is about a soldier and *War Photographer* about a photographer. Neither can forget what he saw, which is how people talk about trauma today.

applications.title: Choosing a pair in the exam
applications.body: If the named poem is *Ozymandias*, *My Last Duchess* is a strong pair: two proud rulers and two works of art. The statue is a ruin that outlasts the king's power. The portrait lets the Duke go on controlling his wife after her death. One poem shows power ended, the other shows power still at work.
